content.text: Check out the master schedule for the first and second rounds of the 2026 NCAA Tournament so you can watch all the March Madness Mar 29, 2026 at 1:13 pm ET • 4 min read Imagn Images We're just two games away from setting the field for the 2026 Final Four in Indianapolis, with a pair of exciting regional final matchups set to close out the second weekend of the NCAA Tournament. While the madness is dwindling in terms of the number of games, the intensity continues to crank up with two exciting Sunday clashes. First, No. 1 seed Michigan takes on No. 6 seed Tennessee in Chicago. The weekend culminates with a matchup between two of the best programs over the last 30 years in No. 1 seed Duke and No. 2 seed UConn. Tennessee is seeking its first Final Four appearance in program history, while Michigan can return to the final weekend of the college basketball season for the first time since 2018 with a win.Here is a full breakdown of the first two rounds of the NCAA Tournament. Be sure to follow the live bracket throughout March Madness. The Blue Devils can reach the Final Four for the second consecutive year with a win, while UConn can make it three trips in four seasons with an upset. 2026 NCAA Tournament schedule, datesElite
